subject.title: [Bug] Session flush blocks write tool completely during compaction

question: Should silent memory-triggered compaction runs be allowed to write non-memory workspace files, and under what normalized path and user-intent constraints?
rationale: The source repro is clear, but the repair changes a deliberate write boundary for a silent housekeeping turn; automation cannot choose that product/security contract safely.

options.title: Keep hard guard and improve recovery
options.body: Preserve the one-file append-only guard, then reduce user pain through clearer progress, retry, or recovery behavior after the flush finishes.

options.title: Allow validated non-memory passthrough
options.body: Permit non-memory workspace writes to delegate to the existing write tool only after normalized path checks and focused tests prove memory files remain protected.

options.title: Add an explicit operator opt-in
options.body: Keep the default strict behavior and add a documented explicit setting or command path for trusted high-power workflows.

recommendation.title: Allow validated non-memory passthrough
recommendation.body: Permit non-memory workspace writes to delegate to the existing write tool only after normalized path checks and focused tests prove memory files remain protected.

likelyOwner.reason: He introduced the pre-compaction memory-flush feature and is the best routing candidate for a product/security boundary decision about silent-turn write authority.
